page: Microsoft Azure D64ns_v6 is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, configured with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via two threads per core under Microsoft Hyper-V. The processor architecture incorporates 260 MB of L3 cache alongside specialized instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX-Tile, and AMX-INT8 for advanced vector and matrix operations. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 4.0 GB per vCPU. Discrete GPUs are absent, and no local disk storage is bundled, requiring the attachment of remote Premium Storage volumes for persistent data requirements.

Benchmark results highlight strong compute and high-concurrency throughput. The server scores in the top 25% of tested systems for PassMark CPU overall, extended instructions, encryption, and database operations. Real-world application benchmarks demonstrate high throughput, achieving 71.06 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and 90.06 GB/sec in static web serving. Natural language processing benchmarks reflect strong prompt processing across small, medium, and large parameter models, aided by the AMX instruction set. Conversely, synthetic uncached memory bandwidth and PassMark memory metrics reflect average to lower-tier results.

From a cost efficiency standpoint, the omission of bundled local storage eliminates excess spend on unused ephemeral disks, directing resource allocation strictly to dense multi-core processing, 256 GB of RAM, and network capabilities. The configuration is appropriate for distributed in-memory databases, high-throughput static and dynamic web serving, multi-threaded batch compression pipelines, enterprise application tiers, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ns_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 64 vCPUs derived from 32 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with 260 MB of L3 cache and hardware support for AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, it pairs compute capacity with 256.0 GB of system memory at a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server features no integrated local storage or discrete GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage. Benchmark results demonstrate strong performance in PassMark CPU suites, database transactions, cryptographic tests, and Redis operations yielding 71.06 million operations per second, alongside 90.06 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. While uncached memory throughput reflects average performance tiers, the instance offers balanced multi-core throughput and memory density well suited for high-concurrency web tiers, distributed cache nodes, data processing pipelines, and CPU-based LLM inference workloads.
